description: I look after the HR system for our board — staff records, leave, claims, and the monthly payroll run. About 900 officers on it plus the contract staff. The payroll part talks to CPF and IRAS for the submissions and the bank file goes out around the 22nd. We've had it since 2016, the vendor customised it quite heavily for us so upgrades are always painful. Only HR and Finance can get in, and the payroll module is separate again — my team of four has access to that. Honestly the reporting is the weakest part, we still export to Excel for anything the director asks for.
persona: HR executive, ~15 years in the service, non-technical, answering a free-text field on a system-owner onboarding form

description:
Hi Wei Ling,

As discussed — the vendor portal is the thing suppliers log into to register, submit quotes for our small-value purchases and upload invoices. It sits alongside GeBIZ, doesn't replace it; anything above the threshold still goes through GeBIZ properly. Suppliers self-register with Corppass and our procurement officers approve them. There's a document upload bit for ACRA certs, financial statements, that sort of thing.

It's on the government commercial cloud and the vendor manages it under the maintenance contract. Which reminds me — that contract expires in March and Finance is asking whether we renew or move to the whole-of-government platform, so don't sink too much time into this one.

Roughly 1,400 registered suppliers last I checked.

Thanks
Siti
persona: Procurement manager forwarding context to a colleague by email; moderately IT-literate, more interested in the contract renewal than the system

description: I'm the one who updates the website — it's the main public site for the board, so all the announcements, media releases, the forms people download, the contact us page. There's a CMS, I just log in and publish. I think it's on the government cloud? IT handles that side, we only do content. We get maybe 200,000 visits a month, more when there's a scheme announcement.
persona: Corporate communications officer; owns the content, not the platform, and is openly unsure where it runs

description: Licensing service covering the six licence classes our division administers — new application, renewal, amendment, and the appeal flow. Public front end is a React SPA behind CloudFront; applicants authenticate with Singpass for individuals and Corppass for entities through the NDI OIDC connector. Backend is Java Spring Boot on ECS Fargate in our GCC AWS account, Aurora PostgreSQL encrypted at rest, multi-AZ. Payments hand off to the whole-of-government payment gateway so we never touch card data. Officers use a separate internal portal reachable only from the intranet, AD group based access, four roles — screener, approver, supervisor, read-only auditor. We publish licence status to the public register nightly and expose a read API to two other agencies over the government API exchange, mTLS and rate limited. Audit logs go to CloudWatch and get shipped to the SOC's SIEM. Peak is renewal season in Q1, about 40k applications a year.
persona: Senior software engineer / tech lead on the licensing platform; names architecture precisely and unprompted

description:
Case management — I inherited this from Ah Kiat when he moved over to policy, so some of this is second-hand.

Officers use it to track complaints and enforcement cases. Case gets created from the hotline or the online feedback form, assigned to an officer, then investigation stage, site visit notes, photos attached, then the outcome — warning letter, composition fine, or NFA.

It holds names, NRIC, addresses of the people involved and sometimes the complainant's own details, which we're supposed to keep separate from the respondent view but I'm not sure that's actually enforced in the system.

About 60 officers across three branches use it daily. Runs slow after lunch, everyone complains.

Built around 2014 I think. There's been talk of replacing it for three years.
persona: Operations officer who took over the system from a departed colleague; writing rambling handover-style notes

description: Our analytics platform pulls data from about a dozen upstream operational systems — licensing, case management, finance, the sensor feeds — into a warehouse we use for reporting and some modelling work. Ingestion is mostly nightly batch via Airflow with a couple of near-real-time streams through Kafka. Landing zone in S3, transformations in dbt, warehouse is Redshift. Analysts hit it through Tableau and a handful of us go direct with SQL. We do hold personal data in the raw layer — NRIC is tokenised in the curated layer but raw keeps it as-is because reconciliation needs it. Team is three engineers and two analysts. Biggest headache is upstream schema changes nobody tells us about.
persona: Data engineer; technically precise about pipeline and tooling, says nothing about access control or retention

description:
I run the mapping system for the planning and enforcement teams. It's basically ArcGIS Enterprise with our own layers on top — land parcels, our asset locations, inspection points, plus some layers we pull in from OneMap and from SLA. Officers view it in a browser; the enforcement guys have a field app on their tablets that lets them drop a point and attach photos on site, which syncs back once they get signal.

There's a public-facing viewer too but it only shows a cut-down set of layers. Where exactly the tile server sits I'd have to check with our infra colleague.
persona: GIS analyst; fluent in the geospatial stack, hazy on the hosting layer beneath it

description:
We've got roughly 2,300 sensors deployed across the estate — water level, flow meters, a few air quality units, and the door contacts on the pump houses. Most are NB-IoT on the telco's network, the older ones are LoRaWAN through gateways we own. They report every 15 minutes, more often if a threshold trips, and that fires an SMS and an email to the duty officer.

The data lands in some platform the vendor runs — I honestly couldn't tell you the architecture, we get a dashboard and an API key and that's the extent of my involvement. My team's job is field maintenance, battery swaps, that side of it.

Threshold config is done by the vendor too, which I'm not thrilled about.
persona: Facilities / operations engineer responsible for the physical sensor estate; explicitly disclaims knowledge of the backend

description:
hi — re your question, the EDMS is where all our official records live. divisional folders, correspondence, minutes, contracts, the lot. everything gets a file reference under the classification scheme and there's a retention schedule attached to each series. disposal is supposed to be automatic at end of retention but in practice someone from my team reviews the list first.

about 4 million documents in there now. it's SharePoint based, we migrated off the old Documentum thing in 2021 and that migration was a nightmare, half the metadata came across wrong and we're still cleaning it up
persona: Records manager replying on Teams; strong on records policy, casual register, silent on hosting and access

description: The intranet's just our internal staff site — announcements, HR forms, the staff directory, booking meeting rooms and the shuttle bus. Staff log in with their work account. Runs on SharePoint.
persona: Junior corporate services officer giving a one-line answer because they don't think the system is interesting

description:
I manage the contact centre — 22 agents on the phones plus four handling the email and webchat queue. We take about 3,000 calls a month and it spikes badly whenever a scheme opens.

The system does the call routing, the IVR menu, the queueing, and it logs every interaction against the caller so the next agent can see the history. Calls are recorded for quality and training and we keep them for a period. Agents pull up the caller's case in the licensing system in a separate window — the two don't talk to each other, which is a daily annoyance.

It's Genesys, the cloud version, we came off the old on-prem PABX about two years ago.
persona: Contact centre operations manager; process-focused, vague on retention period and silent on where recordings are stored

description:
Our public app — iOS and Android, about 180,000 downloads, maybe 40k monthly actives. People use it to check their application status, pay fees, get push notifications when something's due, and there's a locate-nearest-office map that nobody uses.

Login is Singpass so we don't hold passwords ourselves. Users can save their vehicle and property details in the app for convenience.

Small team — me, a designer, and the dev work is outsourced to an agency on a two-year contract. Budget got trimmed this FY so we've parked the accessibility rework and the Malay and Tamil translations, which I'm not happy about but there we are.
persona: Product manager for the mobile app; describes the user-facing surface and the funding squeeze, never mentions the backend

description:
Raising this ahead of the platform review.

Environment: staging for the licensing service. Separate AWS account from prod, same VPC layout, scaled down — two t3.medium app nodes, single-AZ RDS. Deployed from the same pipeline as prod, branch-gated.

Access: whole dev team plus the two QA contractors have console and database access. No MFA on the break-glass IAM user.

Data: we refresh the staging DB from a prod snapshot roughly monthly. The anonymisation script exists but has been failing silently since the schema change in June, so current staging data is effectively live citizen data.

Needs a decision before UAT starts.
persona: Development team lead filing a Jira ticket; precise, and flagging a known problem rather than presenting the system

description:
It's a chatbot thing for staff — you ask a question in plain English and it answers from our internal documents. Circulars, SOPs, the HR handbook, some of the older policy papers. The idea was to stop officers WhatsApping the same five people every time.

The vendor built it. There's a model behind it, Azure OpenAI I believe, or it might be going through the government's own service now, they changed something in July. The documents get chopped up and put into some kind of search index and the model reads the relevant bits before answering — that's roughly my understanding of it.

It shows the source document at the bottom of each answer, which people do click on.

About 200 staff have access in the pilot.
persona: Digital transformation officer running the pilot; half-remembered technical vocabulary, genuinely unsure what changed in July

description:
Billing and payments for our fee-charging services. It generates the invoices — licence fees, inspection charges, late payment penalties — sends them out by email and post, and takes payment through PayNow, eNETS, GIRO deduction for the recurring ones, and card. Card and eNETS go through the gateway and the merchant side is set up under Finance's account, not ours.

It reconciles daily against the bank statement file and posts into the finance system, though the posting fails often enough that one of my officers spends a morning a week clearing exceptions.

We process roughly $18 million a year across about 90,000 transactions. Been running since 2019.
persona: Finance systems officer; comfortable with payment rails and reconciliation, says nothing about card data handling or hosting
